title: Signature Writing Community Rules People Can Follow
body:
The Signature Rule Stone is an original Signature design that carves community rules onto a small set of stones, one rule per stone, displayed where every member passes. A stone cannot hold a long paragraph, so a rule that does not fit on a stone must be shortened until it does, which forces the clarity members need. Stones are changed only by public recarving, so no rule changes silently overnight.

Method. To carve the stones, write each rule as one short sentence naming a behaviour, test it by asking whether two moderators would apply it the same way, and display the stones at the community's entrance. When a rule must change, recarve it publicly with the date and reason, and give members time to learn the new stone before enforcing it.

Checklist.

  • One rule per stone
  • One short sentence naming a behaviour
  • Two moderators would apply it alike
  • Stones displayed at the entrance
  • Changes recarved publicly with date and reason

title: Signature Welcoming New Members
body:
The Signature First Door is an original Signature design that gives every newcomer a door with three signs on it: what this community is for, what its rules are, and where a first contribution fits. A newcomer who passes the door knows all three before posting, so their first post lands in the right place and receives a useful reply. The door is tended by a named welcomer, not left to chance.

Method. To tend the door, name a welcomer for each arrival period, send the three signs together rather than scattered across pages, and invite the newcomer's first contribution in the same message. Reply to that first contribution helpfully within a day, and record which newcomers received the door so no arrival is missed when the community grows busy.

Checklist.

  • Three signs: purpose, rules, first place
  • Door tended by a named welcomer
  • First contribution invited at once
  • Helpful reply within a day
  • No arrival missed

title: Signature Setting Expectations for Moderators
body:
The Signature Moderator Charter is an original Signature design that writes each moderator's scope, hours, and escalation path on a single charter page the whole team can read. A charter that fits on one page cannot hide an unlimited power or an endless duty, and a moderator who acts outside the charter can be asked, gently and precisely, which line they acted under. The charter is signed when a moderator joins and reread when it changes.

Method. To write the charter, name the decisions a moderator makes alone, the decisions that need a second moderator, the hours they serve, and the path for cases beyond their scope. Add a conflict rule requiring a moderator to step back from cases involving themselves or close friends, and review the charter with the team at fixed intervals rather than only after a crisis.

Checklist.

  • Decisions alone and decisions together named
  • Hours served stated
  • Escalation path written
  • Conflict rule: step back
  • Charter reread when it changes

title: Signature Handling a First Rule Break
body:
The Signature First Lantern is an original Signature design that answers a first rule break with a lantern rather than a gavel: a private light that shows the member the rule, the behaviour, and the way back. The lantern message carries exactly three things, the rule, the example, and the alternative, and it ends by asking whether the rule was unclear. A member who receives a lantern knows what to do next, which is the whole point of a first response.

Method. To light a lantern, write privately, name the rule in the member's own words where possible, show the behaviour concerned, and offer the alternative place or form. Ask whether the rule was unclear, record the lantern briefly, and treat the member's next contribution as a fresh start rather than a probation to be watched.

Checklist.

  • Private message, not public rebuke
  • Rule, behaviour, and alternative
  • Ask whether the rule was unclear
  • Record briefly
  • Next contribution treated as a fresh start

title: Signature De-escalating a Heated Thread
body:
The Signature Cool Room is an original Signature design that moves a heated thread into a slower room instead of closing it. In the cool room, replies arrive at set intervals, each reply must answer the moderator's fair summary, and personal remarks are returned for rewriting before they appear. The room's slowness is its medicine: heat cannot survive a pace that gives everyone time to read before replying.

Method. To open a cool room, post the fair summary, set the reply interval, and require replies to address the summary's points in order. Return personal remarks for rewriting with a note on what to change, and return the thread to the open room only when two consecutive rounds pass without an attack. Record the move and the reason, so the room is understood as care rather than punishment.

Checklist.

  • Fair summary posted
  • Replies at set intervals
  • Replies address summary points
  • Personal remarks returned for rewriting
  • Return after two calm rounds

title: Signature Spam and Off-Topic Posts
body:
The Signature Redirect Sign is an original Signature design that replaces a removed post with a small sign pointing the way: the rule, the reason, and the right place, in three short lines. The sign stays visible where the post stood, so members learn the boundary from the sign itself rather than from rumours about vanished posts. A removal without a sign is treated as unfinished work, however justified the removal was.

Method. To post a sign, remove the content, leave the three-line sign in its place, and point to the right place where one exists. Apply the sign to every removal without exception, including removals of established members' posts, and review the signs regularly to see which boundaries members most often cross, since a frequently crossed boundary may be a rule that needs rewriting.

Checklist.

  • Three lines: rule, reason, right place
  • Sign stays where the post stood
  • Every removal gets a sign
  • Established members included
  • Signs reviewed for rule clarity

title: Signature Appeals: Challenging a Moderation Decision
body:
The Signature Second Look is an original Signature design that gives every moderation decision a second look by fresh eyes before it becomes final on appeal. The second moderator reads only the rule, the evidence, and the member's appeal, without the first moderator's reasoning, so the review is genuinely independent rather than a polite confirmation. Where the second look disagrees, the member's version is restored and the disagreement is recorded as a lesson for the rule.

Method. To give a second look, hide the first moderator's reasoning from the reviewer, ask the reviewer to decide from rule and evidence alone, and compare the two decisions. If they differ, restore the member's content or standing, tell the member why, and note the rule or guidance that needs clarifying so the same disagreement does not recur.

Checklist.

  • Reviewer sees rule, evidence, appeal only
  • First reasoning hidden from reviewer
  • Decide from rule and evidence alone
  • Disagreement restores the member
  • Lesson recorded for the rule

title: Signature Handling Harassment Reports
body:
The Signature Safe Room is an original Signature design that receives harassment reports in a room only the handling moderators can enter, with the reporter's words kept intact and the reporter's identity kept apart from the case discussion. The room's rule is that the reporter is believed enough to act on the evidence, and that no step in the room is taken to satisfy onlookers. The room closes with a general outcome told to the reporter, and the detailed record stays sealed.

Method. To hold a safe room, open a private channel for the report, separate the reporter's identity from the evidence discussion, and assign handling moderators who have no personal connection to the reported person. Act on the pattern shown by the evidence, tell the reporter the general outcome, and seal the detailed record so later moderators can learn from the pattern without reopening the reporter's experience.

Checklist.

  • Private room, handling moderators only
  • Identity separated from evidence discussion
  • No personal connection to reported person
  • General outcome told to reporter
  • Detailed record sealed

title: Signature Moderating a Live Chat or Event
body:
The Signature Two Watchers design is an original Signature design for live events: two watchers, one for the room and one for the record, working in parallel. The room watcher acts in the moment, while the record watcher logs every action with its reason, so the event can be reviewed afterwards without relying on memory. The pair trades the speed of a single moderator for the accountability of two, which is the right trade for a live audience.

Method. To staff two watchers, assign the room role and the record role before the event, give the record watcher no removal duties so their log stays complete, and agree on a signal for the room watcher to call for a pause. After the event, the record watcher produces the review from the log, and the team updates its preparation from that review before the next event.

Checklist.

  • Room watcher acts in the moment
  • Record watcher logs every action
  • Record watcher holds no removal duties
  • Signal agreed for a pause
  • Review produced from the log

title: Signature Recruiting and Training Volunteer Moderators
body:
The Signature Apprentice Path is an original Signature design that grows moderators through visible stages: helper, apprentice, and moderator, each with its own tasks and its own mentor. A helper answers and welcomes, an apprentice decides practice cases and shadows real ones, and a moderator acts with a mentor reviewing early decisions. No stage is skipped, so no moderator arrives at full power without having shown judgement at each smaller power.

Method. To run the path, name the stages and their tasks publicly, invite helpers from visible helpfulness, and move apprentices forward only on reviewed practice decisions. Keep a mentor attached through the first months of moderation, and let any moderator step back to a smaller stage without shame when life demands it, since a team that allows stepping back keeps its people.

Checklist.

  • Stages: helper, apprentice, moderator
  • Each stage has its own tasks
  • Apprentices decide practice cases
  • Mentor reviews early decisions
  • Stepping back allowed without shame

title: Signature Transparency: Moderation Logs and Reports
body:
The Signature Open Ledger is an original Signature design that publishes moderation counts as a ledger anyone can read and no one can quietly rewrite. Each period's ledger lists actions by rule and outcome, carries the previous period's closing count forward, and is signed by two moderators, so a missing or altered period breaks the chain visibly. The ledger shows the shape of moderation without showing its private cases.

Method. To keep the ledger, count actions by rule and outcome each period, carry the closing count forward, and have two moderators attest the period's numbers before publication. Publish the ledger where members can find it, explain large changes in plain words, and keep the private case records sealed apart from the ledger, so accountability and privacy are both kept rather than traded.

Checklist.

  • Actions counted by rule and outcome
  • Closing count carried forward
  • Two moderators attest each period
  • Ledger published where members find it
  • Private case records sealed apart

title: Signature Conflict Between Members
body:
The Signature Bridge Table is an original Signature design for member conflict: a table with three seats, one for each side and one for the shared account. Each side speaks first to the table rather than to each other, the table holds a shared account both sides accept, and the agreement is written on the table itself, naming future behaviours and a review date. The table stays in the room after the meeting, so the agreement can be checked without reopening the argument.

Method. To set the table, hear each side privately, write the shared account from what both accept, and seat both sides with the account between them. Agree future behaviours in specific words, set the review date before anyone leaves, and follow up on that date by reading the agreement aloud and asking whether it held.

Checklist.

  • Three seats: two sides, one shared account
  • Each side speaks to the table first
  • Agreement written on the table
  • Future behaviours in specific words
  • Review date set before leaving

title: Signature Protecting Younger and Vulnerable Members
body:
The Signature Guardian Gate is an original Signature design that places a gate between younger members and the wider community's private spaces. The gate's rules are simple and public: no private contact without a guardian-visible channel, no personal information requests, and every report from a younger member receives a prompt, private, adult-handled response. The gate is checked by moderators at fixed intervals, so a rule that has drifted is caught before it fails a member.

Method. To tend the gate, publish its rules where younger members and guardians can read them, keep a guardian-visible channel for any necessary private contact, and train every moderator in the escalation path before they serve. Log gate checks at fixed intervals, review any incident against the gate's rules rather than against individual blame, and strengthen the gate where an incident shows a gap.

Checklist.

title: Signature Closing a Thread Without Shutting Down Discussion
body:
The Signature Closing Page is an original Signature design that ends every closed thread with a page rather than a lock: a summary, a reason, and a doorway to the continuation, written as the thread's final post. The page stays attached to the thread, so any member who finds the thread later finds its ending and its doorway together, and the thread's value survives its closure instead of being buried by it.

Method. To write a closing page, summarise the discussion fairly, state the closing reason in one sentence, and name the doorway where the conversation continues. Attach the page as the thread's final post, leave the thread readable, and return to the doorway yourself to welcome members who follow it, so the closure feels like a redirection rather than a rejection.

Checklist.

  • Summary as final post
  • Reason in one sentence
  • Doorway to continuation named
  • Thread left readable
  • Doorway tended by the closer

title: Signature Moderator Burnout and Rotation
body:
The Signature Rest Roster is an original Signature design that schedules moderation like any other demanding work: shifts, rest weeks, and cover, written on a roster the whole team can read. A moderator's rest week is protected like a shift, with cover named in advance, and a moderator returning from rest rejoins on lighter duties before resuming the hardest ones. The roster makes rest a normal rotation rather than a sign of weakness.

Method. To keep the roster, schedule demanding duties in bounded blocks, name cover for every rest period before it begins, and protect rest weeks from requests to cover emergencies except in genuine crisis. Check in with returning moderators, rejoin them on lighter duties, and review the roster when the team's size or workload changes, so rest keeps pace with demand.

Checklist.

  • Demanding duties in bounded blocks
  • Cover named before rest begins
  • Rest weeks protected
  • Return on lighter duties
  • Roster reviewed when workload changes

title: Signature Reviewing Rules Over Time
body:
The Signature Rule Seasons design is an original Signature design that reviews community rules in seasons: each season, the community gathers feedback, revises the stones, and publishes the new stones with their reasons, before the next season begins. The seasonal rhythm means no rule is ever permanent and no rule is ever changed in a panic, because every change waits for its season unless safety demands otherwise. Members learn to save their rule concerns for the season, where they will be heard.

Method. To hold a season, open a structured feedback period, gather enforcement patterns from the ledger, and revise the stones in public with reasons for each change. Publish the new stones with an effective date, give members time to learn them, and archive the old stones beside the new ones so the community's rule history stays readable.

Checklist.

  • Feedback gathered each season
  • Enforcement patterns reviewed
  • Revisions published with reasons
  • Effective date with learning time
  • Old stones archived beside new
